text: Custom First Control Prompt 是面向 DSH Web 的提示词插件，可在 persona 前注册按顺序排列的系统提示词片段，并把配置的 user/assistant 参考对话作为真实交替消息加到普通会话请求开头。它通过 LLM 请求流拦截实现，不写入会话日志；支持按需包含子 agent。Web 设置面板可编辑配置、预览系统提示词、保存模板并查看请求，输入 dock 也能切换注入和应用模板。适合希望为 DSH 统一固定指令或示例对话的用户；不需要额外密钥或外部服务。

Custom First Control Prompt adds ordered system prompt sections and reference user/assistant examples to DSH Web requests. Its settings panel edits prompts, previews sections, saves templates, and displays recent model requests. It needs no API key or external service.
想让固定的系统指令排在 DSH 人设提示词前面。
怎样给每次普通对话都带上一组示例问答？
我希望把几段按顺序排列的提示词配置成 DSH 的系统片段。
能不能让参考对话只发给模型，不出现在会话记录里？
我想在网页设置里编辑提示词、预览效果并保存模板。
如何在输入框上方快速切换模板或暂时关闭提示词注入？
How can I prepend reusable example exchanges to every normal chat request?
I want ordered system prompt sections that appear before the persona in DSH.
Can I inspect model requests and manage prompt templates from the web UI?
Custom First Control Prompt 的功能「有序系统片段」：将启用的配置项注册到 DSH system prompt，并按 order 参与提示词组装。填写负数顺序可把片段放到 persona 之前。
Custom First Control Prompt 的功能「参考对话注入」：把每组配置的 user/assistant 文本转成真实交替消息，在普通会话请求开始时统一前置；消息只在请求路径存在。
Custom First Control Prompt 的功能「网页配置面板」：在设置页编辑系统片段和参考对话，保存为 profile 补丁覆盖，并可查看当前组装的提示词片段。
Custom First Control Prompt 的功能「请求监听」：开启监听后记录最近最多 30 个模型请求的模型、系统提示词和文本消息，可在设置页或输入框 dock 中展开查看。
Custom First Control Prompt 的功能「模板与注入开关」：保存、删除或应用命名配置模板，并可从输入框上方的 dock 切换注入状态、暂停请求监听。
参考对话会在每次符合条件的普通会话请求中重复前置，因此较长的示例历史会增加每次请求发送给模型的上下文长度。

Deployment-configured prompt prefix. Ordered system-prompt sections render ahead of the deployment persona, and configured reference user/assistant exchanges are injected into **every ordinary conversation request** — as real alternating messages prepended on the request path (`llm/stream` interception, zero session-log writes). Static content renders byte-identically on every request, preserving prefix-cache reuse.

  name: '@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt'

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `sections` | — | Ordered system-prompt fragments; absent or empty registers nothing. |
| `sections[].name` | required | Entry name; the registry sees `custom-first-control-prompt:<name>`. |
| `sections[].order` | required | Render position among all sections. Factory convention: harness identity −100, persona 0, tool guidance 100–199; values below 0 prepend ahead of the persona. |
| `sections[].enabled` | `true` | `false` keeps the entry in configuration without registering it. |
| `sections[].text` | required | Static section text; keep it free of volatile values — any change breaks prefix reuse from the first changed token. |
| `history` | — | Ordered `user`/`assistant` reference exchanges injected ahead of every ordinary conversation request; both texts must be non-empty and free of reserved tags (case-insensitive: `<user>`, `<assistant>`, `<exchange>`, `<custom-history` and all closing tags). Absent or empty injects nothing. |
| `includeSubagents` | `false` | `false` skips sessions whose header meta marks subagent origin. |

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · Configuration：Invalid configuration fails plugin load naming the offending entry: empty text, duplicate section names, or a non-finite order. Per-entry section problems (blank/duplicate name, bad order, empty text) and per-pair history problems (empty text, embedded reserved tags) **degrade to skipping that entry with a warning** instead of failing the plugin tree.

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · Injection mechanism：The reference exchanges are built once at plugin activation into alternating real `Message` objects (deep-frozen, shared by reference across requests), then prepended onto every ordinary conversation request by an `llm/stream` waterfall listener:

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · Injection mechanism：- **Clone and redispatch**: loop-built requests are deep-frozen and marker-tagged (`markAgentLoopRequest(deepFreeze(...))`) and never mutated; the listener clones the request, prepends the seed messages, and redispatches through `ctx.llm.stream`. The clone carries no loop marker, the agent-loop log-reconstruction invariant does not apply to it, and the discarded original is a pure `deriveMessages()` projection.
- **Zero log writes**: seed messages live only on the request path — real turn numbering starts at 1 with no collisions, forks are ordinary copies, and compaction cannot shadow the reference history (every request re-injects it).
- **Scope filtering**: auxiliary calls (`purpose`-stamped, e.g. session-title, compaction) and hand-built requests (no `sessionId`) pass straight through; subagent-origin sessions are skipped by default (`includeSubagents: true` opts in).
- **Panel verification**: not seeing the seed messages in the chat transcript is expected; use the panel's LLM listener to inspect the injected real request (Settings → "Custom first control prompt" → LLM listening, or the dock strip above the

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · Injection mechanism：**Verifying the injection works**: in a fresh session ask a question only the injected history can answer (e.g. "repeat our earliest user message") — the model quoting the configured content proves it. `session.history` shows no seed messages (a clean log is a feature, not a failure).

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · Injection mechanism：**Panel save semantics**: the panel's config editor writes an **id-targeted override** into the profile `cordis.patch.yml` (never an insert, so it cannot collide with the bundle layer's row), updating only this plugin's core row (`custom-first-control-prompt`) and **preserving everything else** — other entries, comments, and legacy rows. While the profile patch carries no row, the editor shows the composed config (bundle-layer defaults); saving then creates the override.

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · System sections：Each enabled entry registers via `ctx.systemPrompt.section()` at plugin load, so it participates in every assembly exactly like the factory sections: variable interpolation, scope shadowing, and the assembly waterfall all apply. Static configured text renders identically in every assembly, which is what keeps the request prefix reusable.

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · What the model sees：Configured section text renders at its configured order position — by default ahead of the persona — alongside the factory sections from [dsh-system-prompt](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).
@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · Token impact：Every section repeats on every request; cost scales with rendered length.

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · KV-cache impact：Prefixes stay stable while section text, order, and the enabled set render identically. Any change can break reuse from the first changed system-prompt token.

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · What the model sees：Real alternating messages at the head of every ordinary conversation request — one user message per configured `user` text, one assistant message per configured `assistant` text:

```markdown
[user]      configured user text 1
[assistant] configured assistant text 1
[user]      configured user text 2
[assistant] configured assistant text 2

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · Token impact：A fixed single copy of the reference history per request (it never accumulates across turns, and compaction changes nothing — every request re-prepends the same frozen message sequence).
@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · KV-cache impact：The reference history leads the message sequence byte-stably, keeping request prefixes reusable.

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · FAQ: how does the plugin enter the composition?：The package declares `dsh.bundle` (in-package `cordis.patch.yml`), and the
reconciliation inside `dsh plugin add` activates that bundle layer — **the
core row `custom-first-control-prompt` (server logic: system sections,
reference-history injection) appears with no hand-written patch rows**. The
browser panel (settings page, dock, LLM listener) is auto-discovered via the
package's `dsh.client` declaration — no separate patch row for the UI half.
`dsh plugin remove` drops the dependency and the bundle layer together.

@wm-coders/dsh-custom-first-control-prompt README · FAQ: how does the plugin enter the composition?：- **Customizing**: never copy a `- insert:` row. Write an **id-targeted
  (non-insert) patch** in the profile `cordis.patch.yml` to override the bundle
  row's config (last write wins) — sample in `cordis.patch.yml.template`; the
  panel's config editor saves exactly this form.
- **Offline junction installs** skip reconciliation, so the bundle layer never
  activates — `install.ps1 -Offline` writes the same two rows into the profile
  patch instead.
- **Duplicate-id warning**: once the bundle layer carries the rows, any leftover
  `- insert:` row with the same id in the profile patch (from a manual-era
  install) = **root-list duplicate → the web fails to boot**; `uninstall.ps1`
  strips both shapes surgically.
section: FAQ: how does the plugin enter the composition?
